scenario.name: Microsoft KB5005413, CERT-FR & CISA DFIR — MS-EFSRPC PetitPotam Coercion (Zeek dce_rpc) & NTLM Relay Forensics (EID 4624)
scenario.overview: Imagine a sunlit city park with green lawns, shade trees, winding stone footpaths, wooden benches, and a tiered stone water fountain at the center. Strolling along the city park footpath like an ordinary afternoon walker, a covert courier sits on a wooden bench near the stone fountain and tapes a coded note underneath the armrest. In this real-world scenario, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the park gate footpath in tiny disguised batches, then moves quietly past the park gate footpath into neighboring restricted rooms. A watchful park ranger at the corner kiosk notices the exact same bench receiving repeated timed drop-offs and logs the suspicious pattern on the patrol board. In this scenario (T1187, Microsoft KB5005413, CERT-FR & CISA DFIR, MS-EFSRPC PetitPotam Coercion , Zeek dce_rpc & NTLM Relay Forensics , EID 4624) at 10.10.4, the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: mS-EFSRPC Bind Over \\pipe\\lsarpc, then coerced Machine Account Outbound SMB NTLMv2, then cross-Protocol NTLM Relay to HTTP/LDAP. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering MS-EFSRPC Bind Over \\pipe\\lsarpc, then Coerced Machine Account Outbound SMB NTLMv2, then Cross-Protocol NTLM Relay to HTTP/LDAP, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on Zeek Event 5145 correlated across the documented kill chain.

stages.description: Strolling along the city park footpath like an ordinary afternoon walker, a covert courier sits on a wooden bench near the stone fountain and tapes a coded note underneath the armrest. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the park gate footpath in tiny disguised batches while everyday visitors and the park ranger go about their routine.
